Serial correlation and heteroskedasticity together

Source: vignettes/combined.Rmd
combined.Rmd
library(fgls)

Section S-4 of the Supplement to Perron and González-Coya (2026) combines the two corrections:

  • F-C corrects for serial correlation: Durbin regression, BIC lag selection, quasi-differencing;
  • F-CH then models the variance of the filtered residuals with the adaptive Lasso of González-Coya and Perron (2024). The candidate covariates are built from the unfiltered regressors (or supplied in z), and the quasi-differenced regression is re-estimated by weighted least squares.

The variance of F-CH is the bias-corrected sandwich of the 2024 paper applied to the filtered regressors (Supplement eqs. A.4–A.5). F-C intervals are built the same way with unit weights.

sim <- simulate_combined(200, ar = c(1.34, -0.42), skedastic = "exp", seed = 5)
fit <- fgls(y ~ x, data = sim, seed = 1)
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> fgls(formula = y ~ x, data = sim, seed = 1)
#> 
#> Method:                 F-CH (serial+hetero)
#> Covariance:             robust
#> Observations:           200 (effective 198)
#> Inference:              normal
#> AR order k*:            2 [BIC, kmax = 12]
#> AR coefficients:        1.3981, -0.4621
#> Non-exogeneity share:   0.011
#> Skedastic fit:          lasso
#> Selected z:             log(x), log(x)^2
#> Lasso psi, lambda:      2, 0.06188
#> df_hat:                 3
#> Variance ratio max/min: 42.7
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  -0.5773     2.5323  -0.228     0.82    
#> x             1.0163     0.1035   9.821   <2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Notes:
#> [1] Covariance: PG26 Supplement (A.4)-(A.5) sandwich (robust), with the
#>     first-stage (Durbin) correction.
compare_fgls(OLS = lm(y ~ x, data = sim), `F-C` = fit$stages$serial, `F-CH` = fit)
#>          term statistic        OLS        F-C       F-CH
#> 1 (Intercept)  estimate  3.0197767  3.4310357 -0.5772954
#> 2 (Intercept) std.error  3.1225187  3.7986467  2.5323070
#> 3 (Intercept)  ci.width 12.2400485 14.8904213  9.9264609
#> 4           x  estimate  0.7746907  0.9815785  1.0162912
#> 5           x std.error  0.8656833  0.2010900  0.1034812
#> 6           x  ci.width  3.3934163  0.7882582  0.4056387

fgls() is the general function; this combined estimator is its default.

The first-stage correction

The Supplement does not write out the correction for the estimated AR filter that eq. (29) of the paper provides in the serial-only case. fgls adds the heteroskedasticity-robust analogue of that term by default when the regressors are declared pre-determined (first_stage_correction = TRUE, the default for exog = "predetermined"). With exogenous regressors it is negligible. With non-exogenous ones, simulations show that it is needed for correct coverage (vignette("validation")).

sim_ne <- simulate_combined(300, ar = 0.8, skedastic = "x2", gamma = 1, seed = 6)
with_fs <- fgls(y ~ x, data = sim_ne, seed = 1)
without_fs <- fgls(y ~ x, data = sim_ne, seed = 1, first_stage_correction = FALSE)
c(with = sqrt(vcov(with_fs)[2, 2]), without = sqrt(vcov(without_fs)[2, 2]))
#>       with    without 
#> 0.04187342 0.03825273

No loss under homoskedasticity

When the innovations are homoskedastic the Lasso typically selects nothing and F-CH equals F-C:

hom <- simulate_combined(200, ar = 0.5, skedastic = "homoskedastic", seed = 7)
fit_h <- fgls(y ~ x, data = hom, seed = 1)
fit_h$skedastic$selected
#> [1] "x"        "log(x)"   "log(x)^2" "cos(x)"   "cos(2x)"
all.equal(coef(fit_h), coef(fit_h$stages$serial))
#> [1] "Mean relative difference: 0.03160067"

Bootstrap cross-check

vcov = "bootstrap" re-runs the whole estimator on residual-based sieve bootstrap samples, using the estimated AR filter with wild innovations. It is an independent check of the analytic variance. The regressors are held fixed, so with non-exogenous regressors it does not reproduce their feedback.

fb <- fgls(y ~ x, data = sim, seed = 1, vcov = "bootstrap", control = fgls_control(n_boot = 19))
cbind(analytic = sqrt(diag(vcov(fit))), bootstrap = sqrt(diag(vcov(fb))))
#>              analytic bootstrap
#> (Intercept) 2.5323070 2.7106793
#> x           0.1034812 0.1042649
